"PROJECT: MEDIEVAL FANTASY RPG — ANDROID

1. GENERAL CONCEPT

Develop a 3D medieval fantasy RPG for Android, inspired by the core gameplay experience of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.

The game should preserve the most enjoyable and recognizable RPG features of Skyrim while maintaining a much smaller and more manageable development scope.

This is NOT intended to be a full Skyrim-scale game.

The objective is to create a smaller, functional, immersive RPG featuring:

- Playable fantasy races.
- Detailed character customization.
- Selectable character classes.
- First-person gameplay.
- A relatively open world.
- Real-time combat.
- Weapons and magic.
- Character progression.
- Exploration and quests.

Prioritize functionality, stability, and enjoyable gameplay over the number of features.

Create an original fantasy universe with original characters, locations, and lore.

2. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Use:

- Unity 3D.
- C#.
- Universal Render Pipeline (URP).
- Android as the target platform.
- Unity Input System.
- Unity Physics.
- Local save system.

The game must:

- Run on Android devices.
- Support touchscreen controls.
- Work offline.
- Target 30 FPS on mid-range devices.
- Use optimized 3D models and textures.
- Have a manageable memory footprint.

Do not implement unnecessary technical complexity.

3. CHARACTER CREATION

Character creation is one of the most important features of the game.

It must be fully functional and available before starting a new game.

Playable Races

Include four playable races:

1. Human: Balanced attributes and versatile abilities.
2. Elf: Higher magical potential and agility.
3. Orc: Greater physical strength and health.
4. Dwarf: Greater endurance and physical defense.

Each race must have:

- A unique appearance.
- Different physical characteristics.
- A racial bonus.
- A distinctive starting attribute distribution.

Physical Customization

Allow players to customize their character's appearance.

Include:

- Face shape.
- Skin tone.
- Eye color.
- Hair color.
- Hairstyle.
- Facial hair when applicable.
- Body type.
- Body proportions.
- Height.
- Additional facial features.

The customization system must use actual character model modifications whenever technically possible.

Do not simply display different character portraits.

The selected appearance must remain consistent throughout the game.

Character Classes

Allow players to select one of five classes:

Warrior

- Strong physical attacks.
- Sword and shield specialization.
- High health.

Mage

- Offensive and defensive magic.
- Increased magical energy.
- Staff specialization.

Archer

- Bow specialization.
- Increased accuracy.
- Ranged combat.

Assassin

- Daggers.
- Stealth.
- Critical damage.

Paladin

- Sword and shield.
- Healing magic.
- Defensive abilities.

Each class must have:

- Starting attributes.
- Starting equipment.
- A unique gameplay identity.
- Class-specific abilities.

Players must be able to improve their character through experience and leveling.

4. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement a simple RPG progression system.

Attributes:

- Health.
- Stamina.
- Magicka.
- Strength.
- Agility.
- Intelligence.

Players earn experience by:

- Defeating enemies.
- Completing quests.
- Discovering locations.

Leveling up allows players to improve attributes and unlock new abilities.

Keep the skill system simple and easy to understand.

5. WORLD DESIGN

Create one medium-sized fantasy region.

The world should feel open and explorable without requiring an enormous map.

Include:

- One main city.
- One secondary city.
- Three small villages.
- One forest.
- One mountain area.
- One grassland area.
- Three small dungeons.
- Several hidden locations.

The player must be able to travel between locations without following a mandatory questline.

Include roads, paths, forests, ruins, and natural landmarks.

The world should encourage exploration and discovery.

Avoid procedural world generation in the initial version. Use carefully designed and optimized environments.

6. FIRST-PERSON GAMEPLAY

The game must use a first-person camera.

Implement:

- Smooth movement.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Jumping.
- Camera rotation.
- Basic interaction.
- Weapon handling.

Use touchscreen controls specifically designed for Android.

Include:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Camera control by dragging.
- Attack button.
- Block button.
- Jump button.
- Interaction button.
- Magic button when applicable.

Allow camera sensitivity adjustments.

7. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement a simple but satisfying real-time combat system.

Include:

- Swords.
- Axes.
- Daggers.
- Bows.
- Shields.
- Magical staffs.

Allow players to attack, block, and use special abilities.

Combat must have functional hit detection, damage calculations, and enemy reactions.

Magic

Include a small selection of useful spells:

- Fireball.
- Ice projectile.
- Healing.
- Magical shield.
- Lightning attack.

Magic consumption must use the player's Magicka attribute.

Class restrictions and spell availability should be implemented consistently.

8. ENEMIES

Include five basic enemy types:

- Bandits.
- Wolves.
- Skeletons.
- Giant spiders.
- Trolls.

Each enemy must have:

- Health.
- Attack damage.
- Basic artificial intelligence.
- Movement.
- Detection range.
- Attack behavior.
- Death animation or appropriate defeat feedback.
- Rewards.

Do not create excessively complicated enemy behavior.

Focus on making combat responsive and reliable.

9. NPC AND QUESTS

Include a small number of functional NPCs.

Each NPC must have:

- A name.
- A basic personality.
- A role.
- Dialogue.
- A location.

Implement a simple dialogue system with selectable responses.

Include:

- One main storyline.
- Five side quests.
- Basic quest tracking.
- Quest rewards.
- A quest journal.

NPC interactions must work without requiring external AI services.

10. INVENTORY AND EQUIPMENT

Implement a simple inventory.

Include:

- Weapons.
- Armor.
- Potions.
- Food.
- Quest items.

Players must be able to:

- Collect objects.
- Equip weapons.
- Equip armor.
- Use potions.
- View item descriptions.

Include a basic merchant with buying and selling functionality.

Do not implement complex crafting or economic simulation.

11. GAME INTERFACE

Create a clean medieval fantasy interface.

Include:

- Health bar.
- Stamina bar.
- Magicka bar.
- Compass.
- Inventory menu.
- Character menu.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Pause menu.

All interface elements must work on Android touchscreen devices.

The interface must be readable and must not obstruct gameplay unnecessarily.

12. GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE

Use a stylized 3D medieval fantasy art direction.

The game should look attractive while remaining lightweight.

Prioritize:

- Consistent art style.
- Good environmental atmosphere.
- Clear character models.
- Readable environments.
- Optimized lighting.
- Reasonable texture resolutions.
- Level of Detail.
- Efficient memory management.

Include Low, Medium, and High graphics settings.

Avoid unnecessarily complex visual effects.

13. SAVE SYSTEM

Implement local saving.

Preserve:

- Character appearance.
- Selected race.
- Selected class.
- Level.
- Attributes.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Quest progress.
- Player location.

Include manual and automatic saving.

14. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Develop the game in small, testable stages.

STAGE 1: CHARACTER CREATION

Implement:

- Main menu.
- Race selection.
- Physical customization.
- Class selection.
- Starting attributes.
- Character confirmation.

The character must be created using a real 3D model.

STAGE 2: PLAYABLE WORLD

Implement:

- First-person movement.
- Touchscreen controls.
- One small village.
- One forest.
- Basic environmental interaction.

STAGE 3: COMBAT

Implement:

- One melee weapon.
- One spell.
- One enemy type.
- Functional damage and health systems.

STAGE 4: RPG SYSTEMS

Implement:

- Experience.
- Leveling.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Character attributes.
- Saving.

STAGE 5: GAME CONTENT

Implement:

- Additional enemies.
- More locations.
- NPCs.
- Main quest.
- Side quests.
- Merchant.
- Additional weapons and spells.

STAGE 6: ANDROID RELEASE

Perform:

- Performance optimization.
- Touchscreen testing.
- Bug fixing.
- Save system testing.
- Final Android APK build.

15. STRICT DEVELOPMENT RULES

1. Do not attempt to develop every feature simultaneously.
2. Complete and test each stage before moving forward.
3. Do not generate decorative or nonfunctional systems.
4. Do not claim a feature works unless it has been implemented.
5. Prioritize actual gameplay over visual demonstrations.
6. Keep the project architecture simple and organized.
7. Reuse assets and systems when possible.
8. Avoid unnecessary external dependencies.
9. Do not introduce multiplayer.
10. Do not require an Internet connection.
11. Keep the game compatible with Android devices.
12. Provide complete and functional source code.

At the end of each stage, report:

- What was implemented.
- What works.
- What remains incomplete.
- Any known bugs.
- How to test the build.

16. FINAL OBJECTIVE

Create a compact but immersive first-person medieval fantasy RPG for Android.

The player must be able to create a unique character, select a fantasy race, customize physical appearance, choose a class, explore a relatively open world, fight enemies, use magic, collect equipment, complete quests, and improve their character.

The game should capture the freedom and identity of Skyrim without attempting to reproduce its enormous technical scope.

BEGIN WITH STAGE 1: BUILD A FUNCTIONAL CHARACTER CREATION SYSTEM. DO NOT PROCEED TO OTHER SYSTEMS UNTIL CHARACTER CREATION WORKS CORRECTLY.
"

messages.text:
"PROJECT: MEDIEVAL FANTASY RPG — ANDROID

1. GENERAL CONCEPT

Develop a 3D medieval fantasy RPG for Android, inspired by the core gameplay experience of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.

The game should preserve the most enjoyable and recognizable RPG features of Skyrim while maintaining a much smaller and more manageable development scope.

This is NOT intended to be a full Skyrim-scale game.

The objective is to create a smaller, functional, immersive RPG featuring:

- Playable fantasy races.
- Detailed character customization.
- Selectable character classes.
- First-person gameplay.
- A relatively open world.
- Real-time combat.
- Weapons and magic.
- Character progression.
- Exploration and quests.

Prioritize functionality, stability, and enjoyable gameplay over the number of features.

Create an original fantasy universe with original characters, locations, and lore.

2. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Use:

- Unity 3D.
- C#.
- Universal Render Pipeline (URP).
- Android as the target platform.
- Unity Input System.
- Unity Physics.
- Local save system.

The game must:

- Run on Android devices.
- Support touchscreen controls.
- Work offline.
- Target 30 FPS on mid-range devices.
- Use optimized 3D models and textures.
- Have a manageable memory footprint.

Do not implement unnecessary technical complexity.

3. CHARACTER CREATION

Character creation is one of the most important features of the game.

It must be fully functional and available before starting a new game.

Playable Races

Include four playable races:

1. Human: Balanced attributes and versatile abilities.
2. Elf: Higher magical potential and agility.
3. Orc: Greater physical strength and health.
4. Dwarf: Greater endurance and physical defense.

Each race must have:

- A unique appearance.
- Different physical characteristics.
- A racial bonus.
- A distinctive starting attribute distribution.

Physical Customization

Allow players to customize their character's appearance.

Include:

- Face shape.
- Skin tone.
- Eye color.
- Hair color.
- Hairstyle.
- Facial hair when applicable.
- Body type.
- Body proportions.
- Height.
- Additional facial features.

The customization system must use actual character model modifications whenever technically possible.

Do not simply display different character portraits.

The selected appearance must remain consistent throughout the game.

Character Classes

Allow players to select one of five classes:

Warrior

- Strong physical attacks.
- Sword and shield specialization.
- High health.

Mage

- Offensive and defensive magic.
- Increased magical energy.
- Staff specialization.

Archer

- Bow specialization.
- Increased accuracy.
- Ranged combat.

Assassin

- Daggers.
- Stealth.
- Critical damage.

Paladin

- Sword and shield.
- Healing magic.
- Defensive abilities.

Each class must have:

- Starting attributes.
- Starting equipment.
- A unique gameplay identity.
- Class-specific abilities.

Players must be able to improve their character through experience and leveling.

4. CHARACTER PROGRESSION

Implement a simple RPG progression system.

Attributes:

- Health.
- Stamina.
- Magicka.
- Strength.
- Agility.
- Intelligence.

Players earn experience by:

- Defeating enemies.
- Completing quests.
- Discovering locations.

Leveling up allows players to improve attributes and unlock new abilities.

Keep the skill system simple and easy to understand.

5. WORLD DESIGN

Create one medium-sized fantasy region.

The world should feel open and explorable without requiring an enormous map.

Include:

- One main city.
- One secondary city.
- Three small villages.
- One forest.
- One mountain area.
- One grassland area.
- Three small dungeons.
- Several hidden locations.

The player must be able to travel between locations without following a mandatory questline.

Include roads, paths, forests, ruins, and natural landmarks.

The world should encourage exploration and discovery.

Avoid procedural world generation in the initial version. Use carefully designed and optimized environments.

6. FIRST-PERSON GAMEPLAY

The game must use a first-person camera.

Implement:

- Smooth movement.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Jumping.
- Camera rotation.
- Basic interaction.
- Weapon handling.

Use touchscreen controls specifically designed for Android.

Include:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Camera control by dragging.
- Attack button.
- Block button.
- Jump button.
- Interaction button.
- Magic button when applicable.

Allow camera sensitivity adjustments.

7. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement a simple but satisfying real-time combat system.

Include:

- Swords.
- Axes.
- Daggers.
- Bows.
- Shields.
- Magical staffs.

Allow players to attack, block, and use special abilities.

Combat must have functional hit detection, damage calculations, and enemy reactions.

Magic

Include a small selection of useful spells:

- Fireball.
- Ice projectile.
- Healing.
- Magical shield.
- Lightning attack.

Magic consumption must use the player's Magicka attribute.

Class restrictions and spell availability should be implemented consistently.

8. ENEMIES

Include five basic enemy types:

- Bandits.
- Wolves.
- Skeletons.
- Giant spiders.
- Trolls.

Each enemy must have:

- Health.
- Attack damage.
- Basic artificial intelligence.
- Movement.
- Detection range.
- Attack behavior.
- Death animation or appropriate defeat feedback.
- Rewards.

Do not create excessively complicated enemy behavior.

Focus on making combat responsive and reliable.

9. NPC AND QUESTS

Include a small number of functional NPCs.

Each NPC must have:

- A name.
- A basic personality.
- A role.
- Dialogue.
- A location.

Implement a simple dialogue system with selectable responses.

Include:

- One main storyline.
- Five side quests.
- Basic quest tracking.
- Quest rewards.
- A quest journal.

NPC interactions must work without requiring external AI services.

10. INVENTORY AND EQUIPMENT

Implement a simple inventory.

Include:

- Weapons.
- Armor.
- Potions.
- Food.
- Quest items.

Players must be able to:

- Collect objects.
- Equip weapons.
- Equip armor.
- Use potions.
- View item descriptions.

Include a basic merchant with buying and selling functionality.

Do not implement complex crafting or economic simulation.

11. GAME INTERFACE

Create a clean medieval fantasy interface.

Include:

- Health bar.
- Stamina bar.
- Magicka bar.
- Compass.
- Inventory menu.
- Character menu.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Pause menu.

All interface elements must work on Android touchscreen devices.

The interface must be readable and must not obstruct gameplay unnecessarily.

12. GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE

Use a stylized 3D medieval fantasy art direction.

The game should look attractive while remaining lightweight.

Prioritize:

- Consistent art style.
- Good environmental atmosphere.
- Clear character models.
- Readable environments.
- Optimized lighting.
- Reasonable texture resolutions.
- Level of Detail.
- Efficient memory management.

Include Low, Medium, and High graphics settings.

Avoid unnecessarily complex visual effects.

13. SAVE SYSTEM

Implement local saving.

Preserve:

- Character appearance.
- Selected race.
- Selected class.
- Level.
- Attributes.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Quest progress.
- Player location.

Include manual and automatic saving.

14. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Develop the game in small, testable stages.

STAGE 1: CHARACTER CREATION

Implement:

- Main menu.
- Race selection.
- Physical customization.
- Class selection.
- Starting attributes.
- Character confirmation.

The character must be created using a real 3D model.

STAGE 2: PLAYABLE WORLD

Implement:

- First-person movement.
- Touchscreen controls.
- One small village.
- One forest.
- Basic environmental interaction.

STAGE 3: COMBAT

Implement:

- One melee weapon.
- One spell.
- One enemy type.
- Functional damage and health systems.

STAGE 4: RPG SYSTEMS

Implement:

- Experience.
- Leveling.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Character attributes.
- Saving.

STAGE 5: GAME CONTENT

Implement:

- Additional enemies.
- More locations.
- NPCs.
- Main quest.
- Side quests.
- Merchant.
- Additional weapons and spells.

STAGE 6: ANDROID RELEASE

Perform:

- Performance optimization.
- Touchscreen testing.
- Bug fixing.
- Save system testing.
- Final Android APK build.

15. STRICT DEVELOPMENT RULES

1. Do not attempt to develop every feature simultaneously.
2. Complete and test each stage before moving forward.
3. Do not generate decorative or nonfunctional systems.
4. Do not claim a feature works unless it has been implemented.
5. Prioritize actual gameplay over visual demonstrations.
6. Keep the project architecture simple and organized.
7. Reuse assets and systems when possible.
8. Avoid unnecessary external dependencies.
9. Do not introduce multiplayer.
10. Do not require an Internet connection.
11. Keep the game compatible with Android devices.
12. Provide complete and functional source code.

At the end of each stage, report:

- What was implemented.
- What works.
- What remains incomplete.
- Any known bugs.
- How to test the build.

16. FINAL OBJECTIVE

Create a compact but immersive first-person medieval fantasy RPG for Android.

The player must be able to create a unique character, select a fantasy race, customize physical appearance, choose a class, explore a relatively open world, fight enemies, use magic, collect equipment, complete quests, and improve their character.

The game should capture the freedom and identity of Skyrim without attempting to reproduce its enormous technical scope.

BEGIN WITH STAGE 1: BUILD A FUNCTIONAL CHARACTER CREATION SYSTEM. DO NOT PROCEED TO OTHER SYSTEMS UNTIL CHARACTER CREATION WORKS CORRECTLY.
"
